stem: A kidney waitlist candidate is temporarily medically unsuitable for transplant because of an active untreated infection. Which OPTN waitlist status category is MOST appropriate while the issue is being treated?

options.text: Active with standard allocation priority while infection is untreated
Inactive due to temporary medical condition
Permanent removal for psychosocial reasons only
No status change is required until the infection has been present for 30 days

explanation.rationale_correct: Candidates who are temporarily not transplantable should be placed inactive so they do not accrue undesirable allocation priority while unsuitable, then reactivated when documentation supports readiness.

rationale_incorrect.A: Active status is inappropriate while a treatable contraindication to transplant remains unresolved.
rationale_incorrect.C: Temporary infection does not require permanent removal from the waitlist.
rationale_incorrect.D: Waitlist status should reflect current medical suitability without arbitrary delays.

references.citation: OPTN Policies — kidney waiting list and candidate status.
references.locator: Kidney waiting list / candidate inactive status

notes: Reviewer: confirm exact inactive-status nomenclature and policy section against the current OPTN kidney waiting-list policy.

stem: A liver transplant evaluation packet shows decompensated cirrhosis, new exertional chest pressure, and an unreconciled outside hospital admission for syncope. Which next step is MOST appropriate for the coordinator to initiate?

options.text: Proceed directly to waitlist activation without further cardiac assessment.
Request cardiology consultation and obtain records from the outside admission before multidisciplinary sign-off.
Remove the candidate from consideration because any cardiac symptom is an absolute contraindication.
Schedule transplant immediately to avoid further decompensation.

explanation.rationale_correct: Pre-transplant coordinators anticipate additional consults when objective data suggest unresolved cardiopulmonary risk. Syncope and chest pressure warrant cardiac evaluation and record reconciliation before suitability decisions.

rationale_incorrect.A: Unresolved cardiac symptoms require further workup rather than automatic activation.
rationale_incorrect.C: Cardiac symptoms trigger evaluation; they are not universally absolute contraindications without assessment.
rationale_incorrect.D: Transplant timing depends on completed evaluation and risk mitigation, not urgency alone.

references.citation: AASLD/ACG clinical guidance on evaluation for liver transplantation (cardiovascular risk assessment).

notes: Reviewer: verify current AASLD guidance citation/year and add a public URL if available.

stem: A coordinator is assembling information for the transplant physician to review a deceased-donor kidney offer. Which of the following data elements should be included in the presentation packet for a sound accept/decline discussion?

elements.text: Current recipient dialysis access function and most recent relevant laboratory values
Donor KDPI, creatinine trend, and procurement timing details provided in the offer
The recipient's personal social media posts about their health journey
Current immunologic crossmatch status and any donor-specific antibody history

explanation.rationale_correct: Offer presentations combine recipient clinical status, donor quality metrics from the offer, and immunologic compatibility data. Social media content is not a standard clinical data element for allocation decisions.

rationale_incorrect.B: Social media posts (III) are not appropriate clinical packet elements.
rationale_incorrect.C: Recipient clinical status (I) is essential context for physicians reviewing an offer.
rationale_incorrect.D: Including social media (III) does not support a clinical accept/decline discussion.

references.citation: OPTN Policies — deceased-donor kidney allocation and offer documentation.

notes: Reviewer: confirm KDPI terminology and required offer fields against current OPTN policy.

stem: During multidisciplinary selection conference, a lung candidate is noted to have ongoing active tobacco use despite repeated education and documented agreements to quit. Which outcome is MOST consistent with standard transplant program practice?

options.text: Proceed to listing because tobacco use never affects lung transplant candidacy.
Defer or deny listing until documented smoking cessation requirements in program policy are met.
List immediately under inactive status without informing the candidate.
Remove the candidate permanently without further discussion or re-evaluation pathway.

explanation.rationale_correct: Active tobacco use is a common relative contraindication for lung transplant programs. Teams typically require demonstrated cessation and adherence to program criteria before approval or activation.

rationale_incorrect.A: Tobacco use is a major lung transplant candidacy concern because it affects outcomes and compliance expectations.
rationale_incorrect.C: Status changes require candidate communication and documented policy-based criteria.
rationale_incorrect.D: Programs usually allow re-evaluation after cessation rather than permanent removal for a modifiable behavior.

references.citation: ISHLT consensus statements on lung transplant candidate selection (tobacco cessation requirements).

notes: Reviewer: verify current ISHLT language on tobacco cessation timelines and cite the latest consensus document.
